title: manuscript-guard journal profile
description: A journal's author guidelines, distilled into something a build can check. Every profile records where it came from and when, because author guidelines change without announcement and a profile with no provenance is a rumour. Profiles are written by reading the journal's own instructions, never from memory.

pointer_form.description: The pointer with {n}, once, where its number goes: "Table {n}", "Fig. {n}", "eTable {n}", "Table S{n}".

sharing_version.description: What the journal lets its authors share of one version of the paper.

where.description: Where it may be shared. Empty: nowhere.

embargo_months.description: How long after publication it may be shared.

licence.description: The licence it is to be shared under, as the page names it (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0).

set_statement.description: The words the journal asks a shared copy to carry.

source_url.description: The instructions-for-authors page this was distilled from.

page_file.description: Where the instructions page is stored as text, from the project's root. Without it, profiles/journals/sources/<slug>.txt, the slug being the profile file's name without .yaml.

page_sha256.description: The digest of the stored page's text, line endings as LF, as G4 prints it: the text the quotes were read from.

quotes.description: For each rule, the words of the page it was read from, as the page writes them, keyed by the rule: limits.abstract_words, structure.required_sections, required_statements.<id>, references, english_variant, blinding, text_recycling, abbreviations.<key>, reporting_guidelines, pointers.<kind>, graphical_abstract.<name>, boxes.<id>, sharing.<version>. G4 holds each to the stored page, and a limit's number to its quote.

manual.description: The rules of the page no gate checks (a running title, the cover letter's contents, the order of the title page), each with its quote, so that none is dropped without a trace.

article_type.description: Limits usually differ by type; one profile describes one type.

english_variant.description: Overrides the project's choice when the journal insists.

blinding.description: How the journal's peer review is blinded, as its own page says. Double or triple: the reviewers are not to know the authors, and the build fails a document that names one of them, an institution of theirs, or their ORCID iD or e-mail address.

text_recycling.description: What the journal says of text its authors reuse from their own earlier papers, in a sentence, as its own page says: Methods only and cited, say, or none. Its quote, under `quotes.text_recycling`, is held to the stored page, and G7 gives that quote with each passage it finds repeated from an earlier output.

abbreviations.description: The abbreviations the journal asks to be defined though G14 would let them stand. `define_statistics: true`: the statistical ones G14 exempts (data/statistical_abbreviations.yaml) are reported when undefined. `define`: these, by name, are reported when undefined, whatever exempts them. Each is quoted under `quotes.abbreviations.<key>`.

figures.description: The journal's artwork rules, read from its own artwork guide. G4 holds each figure the manuscript places to them, as warnings.

source_url.description: The artwork guide these were read from.

confirmed.description: Whether every value here was read on that page, or some were taken from elsewhere and are still to be confirmed.

applies_from.description: When the journal applies these rules. From acceptance, G4 says what does not meet them as notes.

formats.description: The file formats the journal takes for a figure.

min_dpi.description: The least resolution at the printed width, by kind of figure.

max_dpi.description: The most resolution the journal takes.

widths_mm.description: The widths the journal prints figures at: one column, two columns.

max_height_mm.description: The tallest a figure may print.

max_file_mb.description: The largest file the journal takes, in MB.

min_text_pt.description: The smallest text at the printed size, in points.

min_line_pt.description: The thinnest line at the printed size, in points.

legend_words.description: The most words in a figure's legend.

alt_text.description: Whether the journal requires each figure to carry alternative text, or asks for it. Required: G3 fails a figure with none at submission. Requested: a warning.

alt_text_max_chars.description: The most characters a figure's alternative text may hold.

print.description: How the journal prints figures. Greyscale: G3 warns of two colours that print as one grey, which it otherwise only notes.

supplementary.description: Rules of their own for supplementary figures: each one given here replaces the same rule above for them, and the rest above still hold.

formats.description: The file formats the journal takes for a figure.

min_dpi.description: The least resolution at the printed width, by kind of figure.

max_dpi.description: The most resolution the journal takes.

widths_mm.description: The widths the journal prints figures at: one column, two columns.

max_height_mm.description: The tallest a figure may print.

max_file_mb.description: The largest file the journal takes, in MB.

min_text_pt.description: The smallest text at the printed size, in points.

min_line_pt.description: The thinnest line at the printed size, in points.

alt_text.description: Whether the journal requires each figure to carry alternative text, or asks for it.

alt_text_max_chars.description: The most characters a figure's alternative text may hold.

print.description: How the journal prints supplementary figures.

graphical_abstract.description: What the journal says of a graphical abstract, each rule quoted under `quotes:` as graphical_abstract.<name>. Required: G4 notes it while communication/graphical-abstract/ does not exist. Omit anything the page does not state.

required.description: true where the journal requires a graphical abstract, false where it asks for or accepts one.

width_px.description: The width it must be, in pixels.

height_px.description: The height it must be, in pixels.

aspect_ratio.description: Its width to its height, as the page writes it: "16:9", "2.5:1".

formats.description: The file formats the journal takes for it.

max_words.description: The most words it may hold.

max_labels.description: The most labels it may hold.

alt_text_max_chars.description: The most characters its alternative text may hold.

boxes.description: The boxes the journal prints beside the abstract (highlights, key points, research in context, a plain-language summary), each quoted under `quotes:` as boxes.<id>. G4 holds the main text to each: a warning until submission, a failure at submission where the box is required. A box written only in the supplement is not the box.

id.description: highlights, key-points, research-in-context, plain-language-summary, or a name of the profile's own.

heading.description: A Python regular expression the box's heading matches, searched case-insensitively in the title as printed, its number off: "^highlights$", "^key points$".

environment.description: The LaTeX environment that writes the box (Elsevier's highlights). Without it, the id with its hyphens taken out.

required.description: true where the journal requires the box; false, or left out, where it asks for one. Required: G4 fails at submission what the box does not meet.

items_min.description: The fewest items: a line of the box's list, or, where it has none, a paragraph.

item_max_chars.description: The most characters an item may hold, spaces included, as printed.

item_max_words.description: The most words an item may hold.

max_words.description: The most words the box may hold.

headings.description: The headings the box must carry, in the journal's words: Question, Findings, Meaning.

file.description: Whether the journal takes the box as a file of its own or in the manuscript. Recorded for the submission pack; G4 reads the box in the manuscript either way.

sharing.description: What the journal lets its authors share of each version of the paper, and where, each version quoted under `quotes:` as sharing.<version>. Recorded now; the communicate commands read it. Without the block, nothing is refused yet.

source_url.description: The page the sharing policy was read from.

limits.description: Omit anything the journal does not state. An absent limit is not checked; a guessed one is worse than none.

display_items.description: Combined figures and tables, when the journal limits them together.

abstract_title.description: The heading the journal gives the abstract where it is not Abstract: The Lancet's is Summary. G4, G14 and the word count read the section under it as the abstract.

required_statements.description: Declarations the journal requires. Each is found by matching a heading or a phrase.

data_availability.description: The journal's policy on what the Data availability statement says, read from its own page and dated. Nothing is checked of the statement where this is absent.

source.description: The page the rules below are read from.

retrieved_on.description: The day the page was read.

heading.description: Python regular expression matched against section titles to find the statement. Default: data availability, availability of data, data sharing.

forbidden.description: Phrasings the journal does not accept as they stand.

unless.description: Python regular expression: the phrasing is accepted where the statement also matches this, a reason or a route.

identifier_required.description: The statement must name a persistent identifier (a DOI, an accession number, an archived URL), or be one of `no_data`.

identifier_patterns.description: Python regular expressions for identifiers of the journal's own repositories, beside the ones built in.

no_data.description: Python regular expressions for the journal's own forms for an article with no data.

csl.description: The style's name in the CSL style repository, as Zotero names it (the-lancet), or its zotero.org/styles URL. A live build hands it to Zotero; `manuscript-guard style` keeps the file in the project, and an offline build then formats with it unless --csl names another.

latex.description: How the journal takes a LaTeX source, each part quoted under `quotes:` as latex.<part>. G4 warns where a LaTeX manuscript's \documentclass, \bibliographystyle or biblatex's style= differ from it.

class.description: The document class the journal asks for (elsarticle).

files.description: The class and style files the journal hands out, each with its address. The build is to fetch them once into profiles/journals/latex/<slug>/ with their digest and licence, as CSL styles are (DESIGN.md, LaTeX manuscripts, steps 9 and 10); no command fetches them yet. None ships with the package.

reporting_guidelines.description: Checklists the journal requires. Feeds the reporting gate.

pointers.description: How the journal writes a pointer to a table or a figure, {n} standing for its number: {{ref.table.<key>}} prints it in this form, and {{num.table.<key>}} the word of it holding the number. Where a kind is not given: Table {n}, Figure {n}, Table S{n}, Figure S{n}. G2 refuses a form it does not read back as a pointer to that kind of that document.

notes.description: Requirements that cannot be checked mechanically but must not be forgotten: cover letter contents, suggested reviewers, submission portal quirks.
